content:
This deck is the talk version of the post GPU Marketplaces Sell Proof, Not Cards. In 17 slides it covers why benchmark-style compute marketplaces appear, where accelerators outside the NVIDIA line get stuck, and where slicing and scheduling sit in a compute market.

Use the controls at the bottom or the arrow keys to navigate the embedded slides.

Slide: Who Benchmarks the GPU?

Key Topics

Two ways to buy compute: traditional clouds sell certainty, marketplaces sell choice.

Leaderboards: the same model name does not mean the same result, so platforms start selling proof.

Choosing by metrics: prefill and decode hit different limits, and cost is measured per token.

Beyond NVIDIA: software stacks, version matrices and thin public measurements.

Slicing and scheduling: the trade-off between granularity and isolation decides what a card can be sold as.

Missing interfaces: fungibility, device capability claims, bidding meets preemption.
